residue.item: Backdoored third-party dependencies integrated into a security orchestration platform
residue.why: Overlaps significantly with candidate 14 regarding vulnerable/backdoored third-party dependencies in security platforms.

residue.item: Trojanized incident response utilities sourced from a compromised security vendor repository
residue.why: Overlaps significantly with candidate 15 and general security vendor supply chain compromises.

residue.item: Compromised firmware or drivers within dedicated hardware security appliances
residue.why: Rephrases the supply chain compromise concepts already covered by candidates 14 and 15.

residue.item: Malicious plugins introduced through a trusted security scanner’s extension marketplace
residue.why: Overlaps with candidate 14 and 15 as another form of malicious dependency/update in a security tool.

residue.item: Increased high-risk browsing behavior stemming from trust in endpoint protection suites.
residue.why: Overlaps conceptually with candidate 21 regarding reckless user behavior stemming from trust in security tools.

residue.item: Reduced vigilance against social engineering due to reliance on automated threat detection.
residue.why: Overlaps with candidate 21 as another example of reduced user vigilance due to automated security.

residue.item: Hardcoded credentials within out-of-band management or baseboard controllers
residue.why: Out-of-band management controllers are system administration/management features, not specifically created by the process of securing a system.

residue.item: Insufficient auditing and alerting on the usage of emergency bypass channels
residue.why: This describes the absence of a control (insufficient auditing) rather than a weakness created specifically by a security process.
